analysis:
Examined the new ProviderLoop+SelectedModelRecovery.swift (head 1-388) and the ProviderLoop+Serve.swift shutdown changes (head 497, 523; base 522-530).

Recovery behavior: a capacity-tick-driven background loader re-loads explicitly selected models. Eligibility (line 35-42) still requires the model to be advertised, to have no failedSelfTestHashes entry, not to be refused by retirement, and to meet runtime eligibility, so fenced or retired models are not reloaded. Victims (184-206) exclude selected, pinned and request-loadable models, and are rechecked before each unload (119-123, 279). The load calls ensureModelLoaded with allowEviction:false (295), so the existing load gates presumably still apply. Nothing here touches keys, attestation, encryption, cache salt or coordinator authorization (TB-002, TB-011, T-041). On success the code refreshes aggregate capacity and sends a heartbeat (299-300), which affects A-018 routing only.

Add-on hold (TB-012, T-059): the pause check (152) tests servingDrain.refusing. The run() comment at base 24-26 implies a hold sets refusal without refusingForServiceChange. The ensureModelLoaded model-load fence is outside the supplied evidence. Integration should confirm two things: that servingDrain.refusing is true during an add-on hold, and that ensureModelLoaded enforces the T-059 load fence. Otherwise background recovery could load models beside running VMs. The recheck at 139/144 omits isShuttingDown, but it calls the pause reason, which likely covers the drain.

Shutdown: the recovery task now joins the preloads that are cancelled and awaited (head 497). The inline unload loop is replaced by unloadAllModelsForShutdown() (head 523), whose implementation is not supplied. Integration should verify it still waits for modelsUnloading and empties every slot, including a recovery load that finished after the preload timeout. T-010 and T-029 are availability-only concerns here.

No concrete regression is established from the visible source.
